conventions.convention: Specializations are Q-algebra homomorphisms determined by power-sum values. Plethystic −1 has p_k[−1]=−1 for every k; it is different from the ordinary one-letter alphabet with letter −1. A one-letter t has p_k[t]=t^k, whereas coefficient multiplicity c·A has p_k[c·A]=c p_k[A].
σ is a formal series interpreted degree by degree. Hall pairings with polynomials truncate to finitely many degrees; no analytic convergence or scalar evaluation of σ[1] is asserted.

For arbitrary integer sequences μ, s_μ is the Jacobi–Trudi determinant with h_0=1, h_k=0 for k<0, and empty determinant 1. Padding α[n]=(n−|α|,α_1,…) is an ordinary partition exactly when n≥|α|+α_1; below that threshold its Schur symbol denotes the completion, which can vanish or have a negative sign. Missing parts are zero and ∅[0]=∅.

U_n is defined linearly on the Schur basis by U_n(s_λ)=s_{λ[n]}, and U_n=0 for n<0. V adds one box to the first row of an ordinary Schur label, including V(1)=s_(1). stab(α,β) minimizes over n_0≥0 and requires the completed products at every n_0+k to equal V^k of the product at n_0.
The threefold coefficient c^δ_{a,b,c} is the coefficient of s_δ in the ordinary product s_a s_b s_c; it is zero outside |δ|=|a|+|b|+|c| and symmetric in the three inputs.

The FI-module stability argument works over characteristic-zero fields. The theorem extends g_n by zero below the common padding threshold; the prerequisite padded-sequence definition itself leaves those ranks undefined.
A reduced coefficient is the unique eventual value of its padded sequence. For fixed α,β its support is finite. The global product threshold does not assert sharpness for each individual coefficient.

load_bearing.statement: σ[A+B]=σ[A]σ[B]; σ[XY]=Σ_λ s_λ[X]s_λ[Y]=Σ_λ p_λ[X]p_λ[Y]/z_λ degreewise; σ[AX^⊥]f[X]=f[X+A]; and ⟨σ[AX],f[X]⟩_X=f[A] for polynomials f.
For every partition λ and specializations A,B, s_λ[A+B]=Σ_{μ,ν}c^λ_{μ,ν}s_μ[A]s_ν[B] and s_λ[AB]=Σ_{μ,ν}g^λ_{μ,ν}s_μ[A]s_ν[B], with the stated degree constraints and finite sums.

For partitions α,β, R_{α,β}[Z]=⟨s_α[A]s_β[B],σ[ZAB+ZA+ZB+AB]⟩_{A,B} is a finite polynomial of degree at most |α|+|β|, and (U_ns_α)*(U_ns_β)=U_nR_{α,β} for every integer n≥0, including nonadmissible padding ranks.
For fixed partitions α,β, the padded Kronecker multiplicities are eventually constant in a common range, with nonnegative stable values supported on a finite set of partitions γ.
For all partitions α,β,γ, bar g^γ_{α,β}=⟨s_α[X]s_β[Y],σ[XY]s_γ[XY+X+Y]⟩_{X,Y}; equivalently Σ_{α,β,γ}bar g^γ_{α,β}s_α[X]s_β[Y]s_γ[Z]=σ[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ] degreewise, and R_{α,β}=Σ_γ bar g^γ_{α,β}s_γ.
For all partitions α,β,γ, bar g^γ_{α,β}=Σ_{μ,λ,η,ρ,θ,π}c^γ_{μ,θ,π}c^α_{ρ,λ,θ}c^β_{ρ,η,π}g^μ_{λ,η}, a finite sum of nonnegative integers. Nonzero summands satisfy the four stated degree equations.
For every partition α, Σ_{n∈Z}s_{α[n]}[X]t^n=σ[tX]s_α[tX−1]=t^{|α|}σ[tX]s_α[X−t^(−1)], using Jacobi–Trudi completion.

For all partitions α,β and every n≥max{|α|+α_1,|β|+β_1}, s_{α[n]}*s_{β[n]}=Σ_γ bar g^γ_{α,β}s_{γ[n]}, where output labels use Jacobi–Trudi completion and may cancel or coalesce at small admissible ranks.
If |γ|=|α|+|β|, then bar g^γ_{α,β}=c^γ_{α,β}; in particular bar g^{α+β}_{α,β}=c^{α+β}_{α,β}=1.

For all partitions α,β with missing parts read as zero, stab(α,β)=|α|+|β|+α_1+β_1. The full product is V-stable from that rank onward; the theorem handles both-empty and one-empty inputs and asserts no per-coefficient sharpness.

For α=β=(2), the displayed products at ranks 4–9 have the stated ten-term reduced support; the whole product first becomes V-stable at rank 8, whereas the coefficient with tail (2) first becomes constant, with value 2, at rank 6.

concerns.concern: The final Hall-pairing equivalence is attributed to 'the orthonormality of the Schur basis' with a citation to thm-littlewood-richardson-schur-product-expansion. That supplier's Statement gives product and skew expansions; thm-schur-functions-form-an-orthonormal-integral-basis is the exact supplier stating orthonormality. The equality is sound, but the displayed citation should identify the latter theorem.

seams_checked.note: Consumer uses preserve same-rank multiplicities, the normalization z_ρ in power-sum diagonalization, and exact padding domains. The owned completion explicitly extends the supplier's ordinary-partition notation, and its zero extension of g_n explicitly distinguishes the supplier's undefined ranks. The all-rank expansion and global threshold also agree with [Briand–Orellana–Rosas, pp. 2–4 and 8–9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0907.4652).

The consumer retains characteristic zero and finite-dimensional values, uses the constructed padded irreducible FI-modules only on their stated ranges, applies tensor-product finite generation, and then applies the forward direction of the finite-generation/representation-stability equivalence. Finite support is separately justified by bounded weight; no explicit FI stable-range bound is claimed.
